title: Eventual finiteness in an inverse system
statement: Let $S$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $I$ a nonempty directed set, and $(X_i)_{i\in I}$ an inverse system of $S$-schemes with finite transition morphisms [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], hence affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. Suppose every $X_i$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, every structure morphism $X_i\to S$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and the limit $X=\varprojlim_i X_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition] has integral structure morphism $X\to S$. Then there exists $i_0\in I$ such that $X_i\to S$ is finite for every $i\ge i_0$.

proof.text: Write $f_i:X_i\to S$ and $f:X\to S$. By [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], integral $f$ is affine and all finite transition morphisms are affine. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-eventually-affine] with $T=S$ and $Z_i=X_i$: its nonempty directed index, quasi-compact quasi-separated base and stages, affine transitions, and affine limit hypotheses are precisely available. Obtain $a\in I$ with $f_i$ affine for every $i\ge a$. Work on this upper tail. A cone on the tail extends uniquely to the full system: for any $i$, choose $k\ge i,a$ and compose the tail cone map with $X_k\to X_i$; a common upper bound proves independence of $k$. Thus the tail has the same limit $X$.

Choose a finite affine open cover $S=\bigcup_{b=1}^N V_b$, using the affine neighbourhoods in the definition of scheme and quasi-compactness. If $S$ is empty, every $X_i$ is empty and the finite-local-on-target criterion with the empty cover proves the conclusion; choose any index. Otherwise fix a cover member $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$. For $i\ge a$, let $U_i=f_i^{-1}(V)=\operatorname{Spec}A_i$; these are affine by the definition of affine morphism. Set $U=f^{-1}(V)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition] to the open $U_a\subset X_a$: its pullbacks in $X_i$ are exactly $U_i$, since the transitions are over $S$. Its open-restriction clause and affine-scheme clause give $U=\varprojlim_{i\ge a}U_i=\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $A=\varinjlim_{i\ge a}A_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs], $R\to A_i$ is of finite type. The definitions in [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] give integral $R\to A$ and finite $A_i\to A_j$ for $a\le i\le j$, by applying the finite transition to the affine open $U_i$.

For this fixed cover member choose finitely many $R$-algebra generators $x_1,\ldots,x_m$ of $A_a$. The image of each $x_t$ in $A$ is integral over $R$, so choose a monic polynomial $P_t\in R[T]$ with $P_t(x_t)=0$ in $A$. Let $z_t=P_t(x_t)\in A_a$; polynomial evaluation commutes with the ring coprojection, since it is a finite sum of coefficients times powers. Consequently the images of $z_t$ and $0\in A_a$ in the ring colimit are equal.

Apply clause (2) of [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise] to $z_t$ and $0$ at stage $a$. The upper tail is a small filtered category: it contains $a$, any two of its indices have an upper bound still in the tail, and parallel arrows in its preorder category are equal. In particular the two arrows $a\to k_t$ are the same. Hence there exists $k_t\ge a$ with image of $z_t$ equal to zero in $A_{k_t}$. Choose a common upper bound $j\ge a,k_1,\ldots,k_m$. The transition maps send zero to zero and commute with polynomial evaluation, so every $P_t$ annihilates the image of $x_t$ in $A_j$. If $m=0$, take $j=a$.

Let $B=\operatorname{im}(A_a\to A_j)$, with its induced $R$-algebra structure. The images of $x_1,\ldots,x_m$ generate $B$ as an $R$-algebra: every element of $A_a$ is an $R$-polynomial in the $x_t$, and applying the ring map gives that same polynomial in their images. These images satisfy the monic $P_t$ in $B$, because the inclusion $B\hookrightarrow A_j$ is injective. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-of-integral-generators] says that $B$ is a finite $R$-module.

The finite transition $A_a\to A_j$ supplies generators $y_1,\ldots,y_q$ of $A_j$ as an $A_a$-module. They also generate over $B$: in an expression $y=\sum_l c_l y_l$ with $c_l\in A_a$, replace each coefficient by its image in $B$. If $b_1,\ldots,b_p$ generate $B$ over $R$, write those image coefficients as $\sum_h r_{hl}b_h$; then $y=\sum_{h,l}r_{hl}(b_h y_l)$. The finitely many products $b_hy_l$ therefore generate $A_j$ over $R$. This is the explicit argument of Algebra Tag 00GL (lemma-finite-transitive), requiring no injectivity of $A_a\to A_j$. The finite-local-on-target criterion, applied to the single affine target $V$, now gives that $U_j\to V$ is finite.

For each $b$, choose algebra generators of $\mathcal O_{X_a}(f_a^{-1}(V_b))$ over $\mathcal O_S(V_b)$. Their images in $\mathcal O_X(f^{-1}(V_b))$ satisfy monic equations by integrality. Step 4 descends these finitely many equations to a stage $j_b\ge a$; step 5 makes the image algebra finite, and the product generators of step 6 make $\mathcal O_{X_{j_b}}(f_{j_b}^{-1}(V_b))$ finite over $\mathcal O_S(V_b)$. Thus $f_{j_b}^{-1}(V_b)\to V_b$ is finite. Choose an upper bound $i_0$ for $a,j_1,\ldots,j_N$. For every $i\ge i_0$ and every $b$, the restricted transition $f_i^{-1}(V_b)\to f_{j_b}^{-1}(V_b)$ is finite by the open-restriction clause of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-local-on-target]. Composing with the finite $f_{j_b}^{-1}(V_b)\to V_b$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-composition]. The $V_b$ cover $S$, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-local-on-target] implies $f_i:X_i\to S$ finite. This proves the required assertion for every $i\ge i_0$.
